A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FaceLock and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The earlier material can be matched reliably to v2, including the newly added Appendix B.5–B.7.

before.justification: Section 5 and the appendices report original portrait-editing experiments, baseline comparisons, robustness tests, and ablations.

after.justification: The original experiments are retained, with additional FFHQ results, purification tests, and a facial-recognition-component ablation with timing measurements.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same perturbation optimization combining facial-recognition loss, feature disparity, and latent regularization through the VAE. The new experiment without facial recognition is an ablation, not a revision to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix B.5 adds an FFHQ subset alongside the retained CelebA-HQ evaluation. B.6 adds Color Jitter and DiffPure purification scenarios. These extend coverage within the same human-portrait editing task; the existing prompt categories remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain PhotoGuard, EditShield, untargeted encoder attack, CW L2 attack, and VAE attack. The added benchmark and purification comparisons reuse PhotoGuard and EditShield. DiffPure is evaluated as a purification condition.

E3.justification: The added studies introduce Color Jitter/DiffPure preprocessing, a with-versus-without facial-recognition control, and a time-per-image measurement. Existing settings remain unchanged, including the 0.02 perturbation budget, 100 optimization steps, 512×512 images, and 50 editing inference steps.

E4.justification: B.6 extends the earlier blur/rotation/JPEG robustness analysis to Color Jitter and learned DiffPure purification, with quantitative and qualitative evidence in Table A6 and Figure A5. B.7/Table A7 newly isolates the facial-recognition component's protection benefit and computational cost, substantially extending robustness and component validation.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains its five-editing-seed averaging and mean±standard-deviation reporting, and Table A4 retains its uncertainty reporting. New tables provide point estimates, as existing auxiliary tables did; no new repetition counts, confidence intervals, or significance procedures are documented.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–6 and A4 retain their values. Tables A5–A7 and Figure A5 add results across dataset generalization, purification, and component efficiency: FaceLock's FR is 0.356 on FFHQ and 0.371/0.504 under Color Jitter/DiffPure; the new ablation reports 0.534 without facial recognition versus 0.316 with it. These are additional comparisons, not same-setting gains over v1. Under DiffPure, EditShield slightly leads LPIPS, 0.316 versus FaceLock's 0.314.

T1.justification: Objectives (1)–(5) and metric definitions (A1)–(A4) preserve the same mathematical content. No substantive assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the biometric-erasure objective, facial-recognition/feature-disparity approach, metric critique, and performance/generalization/robustness claims. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: B.5–B.7 interpret the additional results as supporting identity protection across datasets and purification conditions, and argue for the facial-recognition component despite its runtime cost. The existing limitations concerning multiple people and emerging generative models remain.

D1.justification: B.7 newly reports approximately 16 seconds per image without facial recognition and 20 seconds with it. Existing pseudocode, hyperparameters, and code/model/data access information remain unchanged. The added studies do not specify the FFHQ subset size, purification parameters, or timing hardware.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations covering FFHQ/StyleGAN, SPIRE, trustworthiness research, and newer generative models. These modestly broaden the surrounding literature; Section 2's substantive positioning against existing editing defenses remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 adds Appendix B.5–B.7, a funding acknowledgment, and corresponding-author information, alongside localized copy edits. Section 5's additional-results pointer changes from editing tools to datasets. The main narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Tables A5–A7 and Figure A5's purification comparison grid. Existing figures and tables retain their visual organization and substantive content, with limited layout reflow around the acknowledgment and references.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the empirical support through a second portrait dataset, learned purification testing, and an ablation connecting the facial-recognition component to protection and runtime. These additions improve confidence in the retained method without replacing earlier evidence. Unspecified sampling, purification settings, and timing hardware limit reproducibility of the additions, making the overall gain useful but limited.
